text:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — seeing ~30% TPS drop on mixed fleet (A100->H100) when running INT8-calibrated models with long prefill (>32k tokens). Logs inlined.

maria: When did this start? Can you paste the perf numbers?

sanjay: Started after the INT8 calibration change rolled yesterday 02:15 UTC. Perf run (single model, 4xGPU pool) below:

perf-bot: perf-run summary:
```
cmd: ./run_infer --model t5-xl-quant --mode prefill_decode --seq 32768 --batch 8 --quant int8 --calib on
TPS:  120 req/s (baseline 170 req/s)
TTFT median: 240ms -> 380ms
95p latency: 480ms -> 860ms
GPU: heterogeneous pool (2xA100,2xH100)
```

lee: 30% drop is huge. Any kernel fallback logs? Could be a code path toggling to fp32 decode for part of the batch.

sanjay: Found this in logs from runtime:
```
[warn] kernel_selector: mismatch kernel (int8_conv) -> fallback to fp8_deconv for slice 3
[info] kvcache: evicting chunk 7 due to memory pressure; memcpy stall 12ms
```

jess: That memcpy stall + fallback smells like our dequant path doing an extra host->device memcpy for H100 due to incompatible packing layout.

maria: Can we repro with perf trace? nvprof / Nsight gave what?

perf-bot: lightweight trace (nvtx ranges)
```
range prefill: 0-1234ms
kernel: int8_matmul    65% time
kernel: fp8_dequant   12% time (unexpected)
cudaMemcpy: 11% time (host->device)
```

sanjay: Hypothesis: calibration sampler produced mixed quant blocks for attention weights, so kernel_selector picks hybrid execution — some tiles use INT8 kernels, some use FP8 kernels; the runtime inserts conversion copy for transitions which kills microbatching efficiency.

lee: That would also break continuous batching heuristics: mixing kernel types prevents coalescing microbatches into larger fused kernels => lower TPS.

oncall: Any mitigation options short-term?

jess: Two quick ones to try:
- smoothing microbatch grouping by kernel type (group_size=0.8) so we don't split batches too aggressively
- force homogenous kernel selection per-request (fallback to safe fp8) to avoid cross-kernel transitions

sanjay: Ran a quick A/B: microbatch_smoothing=0.85 improved TPS from 120 -> 150; forcing fp8 everywhere drops quality slightly but TPS goes to 160.

perf-bot: quick numbers:
```
baseline(int8-mixed): 120 TPS
microbatch_smoothing=0.85: 150 TPS (+25%)
force_fp8: 160 TPS (+33%)
```

maria: Interesting — so we trade some token-quality vs throughput. For longctx workloads, avoiding kernel flips is better.

lee: Long-term: we should make kernel_selector produce kernel-homogeneous partitions and add a dequant fusion pass to remove memcpy. Also need to improve calibration sampler to prefer consistent quant blocks across layers for long contexts.

jess: I'll open a draft RFC with three items: partitioning heuristic, fusion of dequant->matmul, and calibration sampler change. Will add perf numbers.

sanjay: Thanks. For immediate rollback, is disabling new calibration safe? It reverts to previous int8 profile.

oncall: We can toggle calibration flag via /deploy toggle-calib. Doing staged rollouts now for high-traffic clusters.

maria: Please add a short repro script and link perf traces in the PR. Also include the small patch that sets microbatch_smoothing default to 0.85 for mixed fleets.

sanjay: Will do, attaching repro snippet:
```
# repro
./run_infer --model t5-xl-quant --seq 32768 --batch 8 --quant int8 --calib on --trace nvtx
```

lee: Great. Let's sync tomorrow after RFC PR and initial rollout results.

jess: noted. :thumbsup:
